quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
rationale: Section 13 (p0090) contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and free of encumbrances, and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses — expressly including court costs, arbitration fees, settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees — arising from breach of that warranty, which is the operative third-party IP infringement risk. The standard remedy ladder is present at p0091–p0093 (procure the right to use, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify), and the clause survives termination (p0131). The indemnity sits at the fallback: it carries no Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions (more favourable to us than the fallback tolerates), and Section 15 expressly provides that "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14." (p0105), so Garman's indemnity exposure is uncapped rather than limited to a 3× annual-fee super-cap — again better than the fallback. There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, so the walk-away risk of a one-way customer indemnity does not arise. Two points short of our preferred position are noted but not redlined: there is no express duty to defend (recovery is on an indemnify/hold-harmless basis) and no separate refund remedy if none of (a)–(c) is achievable — though the uncapped recovery of all Losses and direct damages for a Section 13 breach materially covers that outcome, and the Section 7/8 rejection mechanic returns all amounts paid in the pre-acceptance window. The ten calendar day notice requirement is tighter than we would prefer but is anchored to a responsible officer's awareness and is not expressed as a forfeiture condition; we would accept it as drafted.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: the inserted grant supplies all five licence qualifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense for Sparkling's business) over the Modifications and other work product, Garman's ownership of its Work/tools is left intact, and the Customer Data limitation is expressly stated. Preferred is not reached for two specific reasons the drafter would need to repair if pressing higher: (i) there is no operative sentence transferring title or assigning the Deliverables/work product to Sparkling (p0088's "No title... is transferred to Sparkling" is retained), and (ii) there is no affirmative sentence that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling data — only a limit on Garman's licence in it. Minimality holds. Each of the three operations is necessary: the grant supplies the fallback rights; the Section 3(c) carve-out is required because the retained sublicence prohibition expressly contradicts the new sublicense right; and the Section 17(a) re-anchoring from "the license granted under this Agreement" to "the licence granted under Section 2" is required to make the new licence genuinely irrevocable rather than fee-contingent. No survival tails, expense language, damages categories or unrelated boilerplate were added, and the Authorized Locations/additional-fee terms of Section 2 were left in place. Trivial nit only: the Section 17(a) edit also normalised "license" to "licence". It sits inside the phrase being edited and is immaterial, but the drafter could leave the original spelling to keep the redline strictly surgical. Intent is preserved: fee schedule, Authorized Locations mechanics, escrow rights, termination mechanics and Garman's platform ownership all survive without contradiction, and the new defined term "Deliverables" is defined at the point of first operative use with no dangling cross-reference. Residual drafting note (not a failure): Section 2's retained sentence makes use of "the Software" outside Authorized Locations "subject to the payment of additional fees". If Modifications are treated as part of the Software once integrated, a counterparty could argue extra fees attach to worldwide use of the Deliverables. The later, specific Deliverables grant should control, but consider adding four words to the insert — e.g. "notwithstanding Section 2, without additional fees" — or expressly excluding Deliverables from that Section 2 sentence, to remove the argument.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties' direct-damages exposure is unlimited; we have added our fallback position of a mutual cap at 12 months' fees. Indemnification (Section 13) and confidentiality (Section 14) already sit outside Section 15's limitations, and we have added gross negligence and wilful misconduct to that carve-out.

ops.text: Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. The limitations of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to a party's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
rationale: Section 15 contains only a mutual exclusion of special, indirect and consequential damages, with Sections 13 (IP indemnity) and 14 (confidentiality) carved out of that limitation. There is no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement (no "exceed" or cap language elsewhere; "fees" is undefined and simply payable under the Fee Schedule), so each party's direct-damages exposure is unlimited and the fallback elements of a mutual cap based on 12 months of fees, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs (neither term appears in the document) fail. The mutual indirect/consequential exclusion and the indemnification and confidentiality carve-outs are already in place, so the shortest cure is one added sentence pair in Section 15 setting a mutual 12-month fees cap — which the existing "this Section 15" carve-out then automatically lifts for Sections 13 and 14 — plus gross negligence and wilful misconduct. This lands the clause at the fallback; we have not pursued the preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, data protection/security, fraud or IP-infringement carve-outs or the payment-obligations exclusion.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

checks.name: cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor

elements.evidence: Retained: "In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages..." — mutual on its face.

Section 14 is identified as the confidentiality section; because the carve-out is framed against "this Section 15", it lifts the newly inserted cap as well as the indirect-damages exclusion.

elements.evidence: No carve-out for data protection or security obligations appears in the rendered Section 15; the only carve-outs are Sections 13/14 and the new gross negligence / wilful misconduct sentence.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetric cap; no retained sentence states Customer's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fees basis; "fees" is used generically (uncapitalised, all amounts under the Agreement/Fee Schedule), so the cap is not illusory.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" (Section 13 = IP indemnity); the carve-out is section-wide and so lifts the new cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same section-wide carve-out reaches Section 14 (confidentiality) and, being framed against "this Section 15", excludes those breaches from the inserted aggregate cap.

elements.element: Gross negligence is uncapped.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is uncapped.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: the two inserted sentences supply the missing mutual 12-month fees cap and the gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-outs, and the retained "this Section 15" carve-out for Sections 13 and 14 automatically lifts the new cap for indemnification and confidentiality. Preferred is not reached and the finding correctly does not claim it: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, no data protection/security, fraud or other-party-IP-infringement carve-outs, and no statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. Minimal: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, the favourable mutual indirect-damages exclusion and the Sections 13/14 carve-out are retained, and the insertion adds no survival tail, procedure, damages categories or other extras beyond the two selected fallback gaps. Intent preserved: the exclusive-remedy sentence, the risk-allocation recital and the Section 13/14 carve-out all continue to operate consistently with a monetary cap; no cross-reference is left dangling and "fees" is used generically rather than as an undefined capitalised term. Verification caveat for the drafter: the indemnification and confidentiality elements rest entirely on Sections 13 and 14 being the IP indemnity and confidentiality sections — confirm those headings, because if either cross-reference is to a different subject the fallback carve-outs fail and must be stated expressly (e.g. "...shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct"). Cosmetic point only (not a deviation): the heading "LIMITATION OF GARMAN'S LIABILITY" now sits above an expressly mutual cap; the body's "each party"/"either party" language controls, but consider retitling to "Limitation of Liability" if the counterparty raises it. Optional uplift if negotiating room exists: add the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and carve out data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP, plus a sentence that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
rationale: Section 20(d) is a blanket mutual bar on assignment without consent, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, and Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning at all absent Garman's written authorization. That is walk-away territory under the rule (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out) and fails every fallback element. Section 17 contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no cure is needed there. We target the fallback: successor assignment by either party on written notice, with consent to other assignments not unreasonably withheld, and a conforming edit to Section 3(c) so the retained use restriction does not contradict the new right.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "any other assignment requires the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — applies to a Vendor assignment outside the successor carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears in the rendered 20(d) or 3(c); nothing restricts the identity of a Vendor successor assignee.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither cited paragraph (20(d), 3(c)) nor, per the review of Section 17, contains any change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, and the redline introduces none.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Either party may assign this Agreement to a successor to its business or assets" — expressly mutual; conforming edit to 3(c) removes the contradictory absolute bar.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "...to a successor to its business or assets on written notice to the other party."

elements.element: Other assignments require consent.
elements.evidence: "any other assignment requires the written consent of the other party"; no retained no-consent exception (no affiliate or other carve-out) survives — 3(c) now defers only to 20(d) and keeps the separate transfer/lease/export/sublicence consent requirement.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: mutual successor assignment on written notice, consent required for all other assignments, and an express reasonableness standard. Preferred level is not reached — no affiliate carve-out for Customer, Vendor retains a no-consent successor assignment right, and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. That is acceptable because the rule permits landing at the fallback, but the drafter should note in the rationale that the position sits at the fallback rather than the preferred. Minimality holds: only Section 20(d) is rewritten (the clause that failed every fallback element) and Section 3(c) receives a narrow conforming cross-reference ("except as permitted by Section 20(d)") while retaining the transfer, lease, export and sublicence consent restrictions verbatim. No survival tail, expense language, notice period or other extra requirement is added. Intent preserved: the Section 3(c) edit is a cross-reference to an existing, valid section and prevents a contradictory retained sentence (an absolute bar on assignment sitting alongside the new successor right); no defined term is orphaned and no dangling reference is created. No change-of-control cure was needed, and none was attempted — correctly scoped.

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
rationale: We reviewed the licence grant (§2), the restrictions on Sparkling's use (§3(a)-(f)), maintenance and support (§10 and its continuation), fees (§11), source code escrow (§16), term and termination (§17) and the general matters clauses, and searched for "exclusive", "sole", "requirements", "procure" and third-party sourcing language. The only uses of "exclusive" run in our favour or are neutral: the licence to Sparkling is expressly "non-exclusive", the escrow licence over the Codes is non-exclusive, §15 concerns exclusive remedies, and §20(h) provides non-exclusive court jurisdiction. Nothing obliges Sparkling to buy software, maintenance, support or any product category solely from Garman, and §3 contains no restriction on procuring competing or alternative products or services from third parties. Sparkling therefore has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, which meets the preferred position; no redline is required.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or accelerated/minimum fee on Sparkling. Sparkling's only payment obligation is the fees set out in the Fee Schedule (§ 11, p0084), and its at-will termination right on 90 days' notice (§ 17(b), p0118) carries only cease-use and certification obligations, with no termination charge. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", early-termination or accelerated fee language returned nothing payable by Sparkling; the only "penalties" reference is in Garman's indemnity in our favour (p0090), and termination for Garman's default actually converts the licence to perpetual and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees (p0128). The § 15 damages provisions limit recovery rather than pre-fixing any Customer payment. This sits at the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is proposed.

rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) and the service-bureau limb at p0039 are ordinary licence-scope limitations on use of Garman's Software and Documentation (no copying, no reverse engineering, no sublicence, no service bureau, use only as authorized); none restricts the businesses Sparkling may operate or the products it may buy, build or license. The Section 2 grant is expressly "non-transferable and non-exclusive", so Garman holds no exclusivity that could prevent us from using or licensing our own products or brands, and the escrow licence at p0115 affirmatively permits us to change, update and improve the Software for our own operations. Searches for "compete", competing products, field-of-use, territory and no-build language returned nothing binding Sparkling. Section 19 is a mutual employee non-solicitation, which is not a non-compete and is addressed (if at all) under the non-solicitation rule rather than flagged twice here. The clause set therefore meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement at any time on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, which sits squarely in the fallback range of 60–90 days, and no early-termination fee, penalty or forfeiture is imposed anywhere in the Agreement (Sections 11 and 17 impose none), so the fallback three-month fee cap is exceeded in our favour. Garman has no convenience termination right at all: Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual so long as fees are paid, and Garman's only exit routes are the mutual insolvency/material-default triggers in Section 17(c); the Section 10 maintenance term is expressly "renewable" with no Garman discontinuation right. That is better than the fallback (Vendor end-of-term convenience on 90 days' notice) and satisfies the preferred element that Vendor have no mid-term convenience right. Short of preferred only in that our notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (a refund of fees for services not rendered applies only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)); these are minor sub-elements noted rather than redlined. The clause therefore sits at (and in part above) the fallback and we do not propose changes.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

proposal.summary: Make the licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: The grant already covers Sparkling's affiliated companies (unconditionally, without any written-notice mechanic), so the affiliate element of the fallback is met. However the licence is expressly "non-transferable", §3(c) bars Sparkling from assigning the Agreement or transferring the Work absent Garman's written authorization, and §20(d) requires the other party's consent for any assignment, so there is no path for the licence to follow Sparkling into a merger or acquisition. That fails the fallback element on a material term. The licence is otherwise perpetual while fees are paid (§17(a)) and is not revocable at Garman's discretion, so we target the fallback only: deleting "non-transferable" and adding a Sparkling-only successor carve-out in §3(c) and §20(d), while leaving the mutual consent requirement otherwise intact. Contractor coverage is a preferred-only point we have not pursued.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is perpetual.

elements.element: A paid-up licence is irrevocable.

elements.evidence: The licence is fee-based with a Fee Schedule but the termination provisions are not in the cited/rendered text, so whether termination is limited to uncured material breach cannot be assessed.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The added carve-outs are limited to "a successor in a merger or acquisition" in §3(c) and §20(d); transfers to successors by reorganisation or asset transfer outside an M&A remain caught by the consent requirement, so the broader preferred formulation is not achieved.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: The written-notice condition does not apply because the grant already covers affiliates unconditionally: "for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations". Coverage without a notice gate is at least as favourable as the fallback, and no edit (and so no duplication) was made.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "non-transferable" is deleted from the grant; §3(c) now reads "except to a successor in a merger or acquisition or as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing"; §20(d) adds "except that Sparkling may assign to a successor in a merger or acquisition." All three blocking provisions are cleared consistently, with no retained sentence contradicting the new permission.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: affiliate coverage pre-exists in the grant and all three provisions that barred an M&A successor transfer (the "non-transferable" modifier, §3(c) transfer/sublicence prohibition, §20(d) mutual assignment consent) now carry a Sparkling-only successor path. Position-complete at the fallback level. Preferred is not reached: contractors acting on Customer's behalf are still absent from the grant, and perpetuity/irrevocability/subscription-termination cannot be verified from the rendered text. If preferred is pursued, add "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant and express perpetual/irrevocable wording for paid-up licences. Minimality holds: each of the three edits is necessary to a single complete fallback level. Deleting "non-transferable" alone would leave §3(c) and §20(d) prohibiting the transfer, and clearing only §3(c) would leave §20(d)'s consent requirement applying to "any rights ... under this Agreement" (i.e. the licence). No affiliate edit was made, so there is no duplicate affiliate coverage; no survival tail, notwithstanding override, or other extras were added; the mutual consent requirement and the Authorized Locations/additional-fee mechanics are retained verbatim. Intent preserved: the new exceptions run only in Sparkling's (Customer's) favour — no new assignment exception is granted to Garman — and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created. "Successor in a merger or acquisition" is self-describing and not dependent on an undefined trigger. Drafting note (not a failure): the §3(c) carve-out is placed inside a clause that also governs lease/export/sublicence of the Work; consider confirming the exception is read as attaching to assignment/transfer to a successor rather than to export or sublicensing generally.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: We reviewed every pricing and commercial location (§ 11 Fees, § 10 Maintenance and Support and its fee-bearing repair provisions, § 20 General Matters, and the definitions/Schedules list) and searched for parity, "no less favourable", best-price, right-to-match and third-party-offer language. The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity mechanic at all: Sparkling's only pricing obligation is to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Garman's charging rights are limited to Fee Schedule rates for specified excluded repair causes. There is therefore no MFN obligation on Customer benefiting Garman, which meets our preferred position, so no redline is required. Note that we likewise have no MFN in our favour, which is permissible under this rule (a Customer-favourable MFN would be welcome but is not required).

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment obligation is imposed on Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Fees are payable only as set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken (§ 11, p0084), additional-location use triggers fees only if Sparkling elects to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations (§ 2, p0028), and maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term" rather than a multi-year committed term (§ 10, p0065). Sparkling also holds an unconditional right to terminate at any time on ninety days' notice (§ 17(b), p0118), so there is no multi-year commitment without an exit. The only volume-type constraints are copy/location restrictions on licence scope, which are not Customer purchase commitments. This meets the preferred position; the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A") is not reproduced in the document, so we would confirm on review that it contains no committed seat, location or maintenance-year minimums.

quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 19 is a mutual no-hire, not a non-solicit: it bars each party (and its affiliates) from hiring "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. No-hire provisions covering all personnel are walk-away territory under this rule, so the clause fails the fallback on material terms. We have narrowed it with minimal edits to the fallback bargain — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no hiring prohibition.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement"; the original blanket "any employee of the other party" (plus affiliate extension) is removed.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of a person's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement" replaces the original term-plus-one-year no-hire tail. Note the retained "During the term of this Agreement and" lead-in could, read literally, keep the restriction alive during the term for a person whose involvement ended more than 12 months earlier; the operative post-involvement anchor is nonetheless the 12-month period required by the checklist, and the total is well inside the 24-month walk-away.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.

verification.notes: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original § 19 was a mutual no-hire covering "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year with no carve-outs — all-personnel no-hire is walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT, so it fails the fallback on material terms and a redline is warranted. The redline is position-complete at the fallback: mutuality, direct-involvement scope, 12-month post-involvement duration, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and an express statement that hiring is not prohibited are all present in operative language, not merely promised in the comment. Preferred level is not met and could not be met by this edit, since a mutual non-solicit still binds Customer; that is acceptable because a clause sitting at the fallback is the intended landing zone here. Minimality holds: the deletions (all-employee scope, affiliate hiring extension, six-month former-employee lookback, one-year post-term tail) are each required to reach the direct-involvement, no-hire and 12-month elements; no survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or other extraneous term was added. Intent preserved: the clause remains a single self-contained covenant with no dangling cross-reference or undefined term, and no other commercial mechanic is disturbed. Optional tightening (not a failure): consider deleting "During the term of this Agreement and" or recasting as "during the term and for twelve (12) months after the end of a person's involvement, whichever ends later than 12 months after involvement ends is excluded", so the term-based lead-in cannot be read to extend the restriction beyond 12 months after a person's involvement ends.

quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
rationale: There is no automatic-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "renew", "automatic/automatically/extend/successive" and "increase/uplift/CPI/adjust" return only § 10, which grants Maintenance Services for a "renewable one-year term" — renewal is optional and depends on Sparkling continuing to pay maintenance fees, so no evergreen roll-over, no multi-year renewal term, and no non-renewal notice window is imposed on us (the walk-away triggers of a >90-day window or automatic multi-year renewal are absent). Because renewal is not automatic, each conditional fallback element (≤60-day non-renewal notice window; ≤5% uplift) and the corresponding preferred conditional elements are satisfied vacuously, and no unilateral Vendor price-increase right exists to cap. The licence term itself is favourable to us: § 17(a) runs perpetually while fees are paid and § 17(b) lets Sparkling exit on 90 days' notice. Rationale note only: § 10 does not expressly state that renewal requires mutual written agreement, and any renewal pricing sits in the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A", not in the reviewed text), so we should confirm the schedule contains no uplift formula; neither point is a material failure and no redline is warranted.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: expiry-or-termination trigger, a 90-day floor of transition assistance, and export/delivery of all Sparkling data within 30 days of the triggering event. Preferred level is not reached: no six-month assistance period, no "then-current rates" pricing basis, no machine-readable format requirement, and no Garman certification of deletion after return. Minimal: a single concise insertion into the termination section for a genuinely missing clause; no existing words (including the Customer-side certification in Section 17(b) and the perpetual-licence/fee-refund mechanics) were deleted or paraphrased, and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense language or procedures were added. Preserves intent: the new paragraph is purely additive, uses only defined party names, creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict Section 17(b)'s obligation for Sparkling to return Software, Documentation and Codes or Section 16/18 mechanics. rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision anywhere: searches for "insurance"/coverage return nothing, and § 20 General Matters (p0135-p0147, p0149-p0150) runs from time-of-essence through entire agreement without an insurance covenant. Garman nonetheless converts and processes Sparkling's data (§ 4(b), p0042) and performs installation, training and implementation work at our Authorized Locations, which is walk-away territory under the rule. We therefore insert a short insurance paragraph at the preferred level (CGL USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, E&O USD 2,000,000, cyber and privacy USD 5,000,000 where Garman processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling, and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request), and can settle at the fallback of E&O USD 1,000,000 and cyber USD 2,000,000.

verification.notes: All six preferred elements are rendered in operative language as new subsection (k); the preferred level is complete and the fallback floors are exceeded as a consequence. Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing provision, and the drafter omitted the model-language extras ("at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail) that would otherwise have failed minimality. No existing words were deleted or paraphrased — retained paragraphs (b), (i) and (j) are unchanged. The cyber trigger is drafted as "any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling," which satisfies the requirement that the Customer Data trigger cover every category rather than selected named data types. Intent is preserved: the new subsection is additive within the General Matters series, creates no undefined terms or dangling cross-references, and does not contradict any retained allocation, remedy or commercial mechanic. Note only (not a defect): the clause does not state "at its own expense" or a post-term maintenance period; neither is a checklist element, so their absence is correct for minimality.
